R941.note: Parameterized SqlCommand with @ownerName; closes injection cleanly, no other behavior change.

R942.note: Standard null-check on weak_ptr::lock() result; matches contract (send once, skip expired, no lifetime extension).

R943.note: Allowlist of columns/directions for Order(); rejects unknown input to empty (no ORDER BY) rather than erroring, consistent with contract.

R944.note: Fully closes CSharpScript RCE but the 'fix' ignores the actual expression parameter entirely, hardcoding Total+Tax regardless of the requested formula - breaks distinct approved formulas required by the contract; write-up does note a 'second-layer fix' is needed for arbitrary formulas.

R945.note: allowed_classes restricted to ShoppingCart; matches existing instanceof fallback exactly, no behavior change for valid/invalid payloads.

R946.note: Moves param into LDAP positional filter placeholder {0}; framework escapes it. Matches sink's parameterization mechanism.

R947.note: EF Core's ExecuteSqlRawAsync has no FormattableString overload (that overload belongs to ExecuteSqlInterpolatedAsync) and FormattableString has no implicit conversion to string, so the fixed code as written does not compile.

R948.note: Extension allowlist+denylist plus UUID filename; response message format unchanged, only the reported path text differs, which is the stated/intended change.

R949.note: secrets.randbelow() with correct inclusive-range offset formula; preserves original min/max semantics.

R950.note: Replaces preg_replace /e eval with preg_replace_callback + call_user_func($formatter, ...), but $formatter is still fully attacker-controlled and unvalidated in the shipped code (whitelist only mentioned as optional 'additional hardening'), so arbitrary PHP function invocation (e.g. system) remains live; write-up incorrectly claims the code injection vector is eliminated.

R951.note: Extension allowlist blocks dangerous types before write; residual path-traversal-via-filename risk is explicitly disclosed as an optional further hardening, not required by the reported CWE-434 finding.

R952.note: Appends File.separator to BASE_DIR before startsWith check; canonical sibling-directory bypass fix, no other behavior change.

R953.note: JsonSerializer<SessionData> is the right general pattern to block arbitrary type construction, but it silently swaps the wire format from binary to JSON, breaking any legitimate BinaryFormatter-serialized caller; write-up does disclose a DataContractSerializer/KnownType alternative for binary compatibility as a fallback.

R954.note: crypto.randomUUID() + detected.ext replaces attacker filename; response JSON shape (url) and 400 error shape both preserved per contract.

R955.note: Adds UseAntiforgery() middleware plus explicit ValidateRequestAsync() call for the JSON-bound minimal API endpoint, matching documented ASP.NET Core guidance; success/auth path preserved per contract.

R956.note: Extension allowlist + crypto/rand filename correctly closes CWE-434, but the write-up never updates avatar_lookup.go's ReadAvatarBytes(originalFilename), which still looks up files by the original name - silently breaks retrieval for every new upload despite the contract explicitly requiring the read path be updated in step with the write path.

R957.note: Adds .RequireAuthorization() to the minimal API route, matching the sibling banUserHandler/unbanUserHandler pattern; no other behavior change.

R958.note: Swaps libxmljs for sax-based xml2js, which cannot resolve external entities; response shape and 400 handling for malformed/missing-id XML preserved.

R959.note: fgets() closes the stack overflow, but the fix never detects fgets truncation on an over-long line and never drains the remainder from stdin, so an over-long input silently returns 0 (success) with truncated data instead of the contract-required -1, and leftover bytes corrupt the next call's read - exactly what the contract calls out and the write-up never addresses.

R960.note: Removes @csrf_exempt so CsrfViewMiddleware re-applies; all three contract response shapes (queued/401/405) are untouched.

R961.note: Adds a precise pre-strcat length check (>= sizeof(path), correctly accounting for the NUL terminator) before concatenation; rejects overlong input, no other behavior change.

R962.note: text() with :date_filter bind parameter replaces f-string interpolation; standard SQLAlchemy parameterization, same query semantics.

R963.note: allowed_classes=>false blocks gadget objects for legacy serialized rows, but the contract explicitly requires loadCart to also return correct contents for rows already migrated to JSON - the fix never handles a JSON-format cart_data value at all, so unserialize() on JSON data returns false, violating the declared array return type and silently losing/crashing on migrated carts.

R964.note: password_verify() plus dummy-hash timing mitigation is the correct pattern, but it assumes passwords are already bcrypt-hashed in the DB; as shown it breaks every existing login against the still-plaintext password column until a separate hashing migration ships - which the write-up does explicitly call out as a required companion change.

R965.note: Removing the bypassing SignatureValidator restores real signature validation, closing the core vulnerability; the added ValidAlgorithms=HmacSha256 is hardcoded as a literal in the sample fix and could silently reject legitimate tokens if the real issuer (Authority-based OIDC) actually signs with RS256, a risk only softly flagged via an inline 'e.g.' comment.

R966.note: Rejects any '/', '\\', or '://' plus realpath()-based containment check; closes both traversal and stream-wrapper bypass; single-filename-only restriction is stated plainly.

R967.note: Path.Join (which, unlike Combine, does not let a rooted second argument override the base) plus GetFullPath/GetRelativePath containment check; rejects escapes, preserves legitimate relative access.

R968.note: Cleanly reassigns ownership so validate_and_normalize never frees req, and process_request frees exactly once on every path; fixes the UAF without changing return codes or logging.

R969.note: Adds secure=True to set_cookie; minimal, correct, no other behavior change.

R970.note: SortColumn allowlist enum resolved in the service layer before the value ever reaches the ${sort} substitution; tenantId binding, default created_at sort, and legitimate sort values all preserved per contract.

R971.note: Replaces file-reading lookupRate with a fixed in-memory rate dictionary; unknown keys throw rather than reading arbitrary files, matching the contract exactly while leaving legitimate arithmetic Eval() intact.

R972.note:
th:text blanket-escapes all HTML, but the contract requires intentionally-supported rich-text tags to render after allowlist sanitization (e.g. JSoup) rather than being stripped outright; the sample body itself is a

tag, so existing formatted announcements will now render as literal escaped tag text - a real regression the write-up only mentions as an optional 'if genuinely required' aside rather than the contract's stated requirement.

R973.note: Wraps the route with the existing requireAdmin middleware, matching the sibling ban/unban registrations exactly.

R974.note: Replaces raw CRLF-vulnerable socket protocol text with Apache Commons Net FTPClient's structured retrieveFileStream API, matching the repo's own stated CWE-77/Java guidance; return type and overall stub behavior preserved.

R975.note: Bounds check on unsigned playerIndex against MAX_PLAYERS before the write; silently drops out-of-range updates, consistent with the function's existing void/no-error-reporting contract.

R976.note: Removes the attacker-influenced decoder.Entity population entirely; Go's xml.Decoder has no legitimate use for it here and none is exercised downstream, so nothing observable is lost.

R977.note: Adds bcrypt.compare() against a stored hash before authenticating; assumes a passwordHash field, which is explicitly disclosed as an assumption to verify.

R978.note: Explicit allowlist array maps command name to handler; only two known strings are ever invoked, and unknown commands return a clear message instead of crashing (improvement over the original's likely fatal error).

R979.note: ProcessBuilder with host/count as separate array arguments instead of cmd.exe /c string; avoids shell parsing entirely while preserving the same ping invocation and output handling.

R980.note: Allowlist map restricts the executable name to four known diagnostic tools before exec.Command(); matches the documented intended tool set, output/behavior otherwise unchanged.
